newsitem.title: GERMANY: Traub says Index, administrator agree takeover.
newsitem.headline: Traub says Index, administrator agree takeover.

text.p: Bankrupt German machine tool-maker Traub AG said on Monday its administrator and the Esslingen-based Index-Werke had agreed a takeover plan that had also gained the approval of a committee of Traub's creditors.
A rival proposal by machine-manufacturer Gildemeister AG, which would have saved more jobs at Traub's main plant in Reichenbach, had been rejected by the banks, a Traub spokesman said.
Traub currently has some 750 workers, of whom Index is expected to keep 450.
Both Traub and Index are leading manufacturers of motorised lathes.

Index last year increased its turnover by 10 percent to 440 million marks ($261 million), with some 1,550 staff. Traub earlier initiated bankruptcy proceedings following the failure of efforts to scale back debt with creditors.
